texts.preamble: Brig. Thota Ramaiah, vs The State Of Telangana on 15 April, 2024 Author: T. Vinod Kumar Bench: T. Vinod Kumar The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar Writ Petition No.13532 of 2023 Order:
texts.facts: This Writ Petition is filed for issuance of a Writ of Mandamus to declare the inaction of respondent No.3 in taking action against respondent No.4 despite petitioners' complaint dated 10-04-2023 through respondent No.5 and representation dated 02-05-2023 as illegal, arbitrary, unjust and violative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India. 4. The case of the petitioners, as set out in the affidavit in brief is that 1st petitioner is the absolute owner and possessor of plot R/o.4-200/1A, Eshwaripuri Colony, Sainikpuri, Kapra, Medchal- Malkajgiri District, Secunderabad, and similarly petitioner Nos.2 to 6 are the absolute owners and possessors of their respective properties situated in Sanikpuri, Secunderabad, within the layout of Armed Forces Officers' Cooperative Housing Society Limited, Sainikpuri, Secunderabad. 5. Petitioners further contend that the 4th respondent, who is the owner of plot No.B-145 of the aforesaid Society, had leased out his property to a third party for running a restaurant/cafeteria and the said third party is undertaking constructions for commencing of commercial operations from the premises/plot which is a residential colony. 6. Petitioners further contend that on noticing the 4th respondent undertaking the aforesaid activity, they had initially submitted a representation/complaint on 07-04-2023 to the 5th respondent-Association through which the lay-out developed and plots therein having been sold to its members. Brig. Thota Ramaiah, vs The State Of Telangana on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151291930/ 1 7. Petitioners further contend that the 5th respondent, on the basis of the aforesaid representation submitted by them, had addressed letter dated 10-04-2023 to the 3rd respondent and requested the 3rd respondent not to permit any commercial activity and also not to give any permission/license in favour of the 4th respondent. 8. Petitioners further contend that despite they approaching the 5th respondent and submitting letter dated 07-04-2023, on the basis of which the 5th respondent making a request to the 3rd respondent vide letter dated 10-04-2023 not to grant any permission in respect of the subject property, the 4th respondent has illegally started the work of setting up a cafeterias as well as restaurant causing disturbance to the petitioners, who are residents of that locality. 10. When the Writ Petition was taken up for hearing on 27-07-2023, learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.2 and 3, by placing written instructions under the signature of 3rd respondent, had stated that the respondent authorities have demolished the illegal and unauthorized structures raised by the 4th respondent on 24-06-2023 duly taking police assistance and photographs taken during the course of demolition of unauthorized structures. This Court on the aforesaid statement being made, had noted that since the respondent authorities claim to have demolished/removed the unauthorized temporary structures, further directed the respondent authorities to verify whether any unauthorized temporary structures are still to be removed and file counter- affidavit by the next date of hearing. 11. On 27-07-2023, though this Court directed the respondent authorities to file counter-affidavit, no counter-affidavit is filed till date. 12. On the other hand, the 4th respondent, who is alleged to have been making unauthorized and illegal constructions, has filed counter-affidavit. 13. By the counter-affidavit, the 4th respondent claims that as per G.O.Ms.No.288 dated 03-04-2008, restaurants/eating places are permitted in the residential zone.
texts.arguments: 9. Petitioners further contend that the 3rd respondent, in spite of receiving letter/representation from the 5th respondent dated 10-04-2023, did not initiate any action against the unauthorized structures being laid by the 4th respondent and as such, the petitioners once again submitted a representation dated 02-05-2023 to the 2nd respondent bringing to the notice of the said authority the unauthorized and illegal construction being made by the 4th respondent, and in spite of the same, no action is taken and hence, the present Writ petition. 14. The 4th respondent further claims that he had obtained registration certificate number under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India as issued by the Government of Telangana and also obtained certificate of registration from the Labour Department and as such, the setting of cafeteria/canteen in the subject premises cannot be objected to by the petitioners. 15.
